title: P-02: PAH binding and reporter model results
question: What follows from the project's existing assumed model inputs?
materials: Stored source_assumptions.json; original model scripts preserved as inert equation/provenance records.
No fitted parameters or new experimental data.
methods: Analytical single-site occupancy and fixed-ligand approach to equilibrium.
Source reporter ODE integrated by DOP853 (rtol 1e-8; atol 1e-10) on a one-minute output grid.
Deterministic competitive occupancy at assigned free concentrations; no score-to-Kd conversion.
results: Reporter sampled maximum: 9.9333 simulated h; ideal pyrene ratio at 100 nM=1.1500.
Model 3 mixture: pyrene fraction=0.045218, unbound=0.678273; competitor half-site=422.3 nM.
conclusion: At Kd = free ligand = 100 nM, the binding model gives t95 = 24.964 min. The reporter reaches its sampled maximum at 9.933 simulated hours. Fixed competitors shift pyrene half occupancy from 300.0 to 422.3 nM; mixture pyrene occupancy is 0.04522 and the unbound fraction is 0.67827.

figures.caption: Conditional binding curves, reporter accumulation and pyrene competition under stored assumptions. All times are simulated; lines are not measured data.

references: Stored source_assumptions.json: explicit source-derived parameter transcription; source hashes and complete parameters are in source_manifest.json.
scope_and_assumptions: Affinities, concentrations and rates are fixed source-assigned parameters. The calculations assume one site, fixed free ligand, mutually exclusive competition and no depletion. The reporter represents an E. coli CFP/YFP model. Results are numerical consequences of these equations and parameters, rather than fitted measurements of yeast or cadmium performance.
